questions.question: How do commercial banks promote trade and commerce? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• How do commercial banks promote trade and commerce? [U] / [CO1]
  • Commercial banks provide credit, loans, and overdraft facilities that help businesses meet their
  • working capital needs. They also offer payment services, trade finance, and foreign exchange
  • support, enabling smooth business transactions. These services collectively promote trade and
  • commercial activities.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: How do mutual funds act as a para-banking service ? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• How do mutual funds act as a para-banking service? [An] / [CO2]
  • Mutual funds mobilise savings from the public and invest them in diversified financial
  • instruments. They offer liquidity, safety, and professional management similar to banks, but
  • without providing direct loans or deposits. Thus, they complement banking services by offering
  • investment avenues.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Mention two feature of NEFT. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Mention two features of NEFT. [A] / [CO3]
  • • 24×7 Availability – NEFT operates round the clock, including Sundays and bank
  • holidays.
  • • Batch-wise Settlement – Transactions are processed in batches at regular intervals.
  • • No Minimum or Maximum Limit – NEFT has no minimum or maximum amount for
  • fund transfer.
  • • One-to-One Transfer – It supports secure bank-to-bank and person-to-person transfers.
  • • Nationwide Coverage – Available across all NEFT-enabled bank branches in India.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: State any two causes of NPAs. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• State any two causes of NPAs. [U] / [CO4]
  • • Poor credit appraisal leading to loans being given to financially weak or unsuitable
  • borrowers.
  • • Economic slowdown or recession reducing the repayment capacity of borrowers.
  • • Business failures due to competition, management issues, or market changes.
  • • Wilful default, where borrowers intentionally avoid repayment.
  • • Natural calamities affecting agriculture and related sectors.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is meant by monetary policy? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is meant by monetary policy? [K] / [CO1]
  • Monetary policy refers to the actions taken by the Reserve Bank of India to regulate money
  • supply, interest rates, and credit availability. Its main goal is to maintain price stability and
  • support economic growth.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Mention two features of banking. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Mention two features of banking. [K] / [CO1]
  • Accepting Deposits – Banks accept savings, current, and fixed deposits from the public.
  • Providing Loans and Advances – Banks lend money to individuals, businesses, and industries.
  • Payment and Settlement Services – Banks offer fund transfers like NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, an d
  • cheque clearance.
  • Agency Functions – Banks act as agents by collecting bills, paying taxes, and handling
  • remittances.
  • Safety and Security of Funds – Banks ensure the safe custody of money and provide financial
  • services with trust and reliability.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is mean by overdraft facility in corporate banking? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is meant by overdraft facility in corporate banking? [U] / [CO2]
  • An overdraft allows corporate customers to withdraw more money than what is available in
  • their current account. It provides short -term liquidity support to meet urgent financial
  • commitments. Interest is charged only on the amount overdrawn.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: State two advantage of mobile banking. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• State two advantages of mobile banking. [A] / [CO3]
  • • 24×7 Convenience – Customers can perform transactions anytime and from anywhere.
  • • Time-Saving – It reduces the need to visit bank branches for basic services.
  • • Instant Transactions – Funds can be transferred quickly through NEFT, IMPS, or UPI.
  • • Access to Multiple Services – Balance check, bill payments, mini statements, and
  • mobile recharge can be done easily.
  • • Cost-Effective – Mobile banking often reduces transaction costs for both banks and
  • customers.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Expand KYC and explain its meaning / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Expand KYC and explain its meaning. [U] / [CO4]
  • KYC stands for Know Your Customer. It is a process used by banks to verify the identity and
  • address of customers to prevent fraud, money laundering, and financial crimes.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: When did the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 come into force, and why was it necessary? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• When did the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 come into force, and why was it
  • necessary? [U] / [CO4]
  • The Act came into force on 16th March 1949. It was necessary to regulate banking operations,
  • ensure financial stability, and protect depositors through proper supervision of banks.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain Reverse repo rate / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain Reverse Repo Rate. [K] / [CO1]
  • The reverse repo rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks. It
  • is used to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system and control inflation.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain current account / [CO2] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain current account. [U] / [CO2]
  • A current account is a bank account primarily meant for businesses and individuals who make
  • frequent transactions. It offers unlimited withdrawals and deposits but usually does not provide
  • interest. It supports smooth day-to-day business operations.

questions.question: Explain Fin Tech and discuss the impact of Fin Tech on traditional banking. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain FinTech and discuss the impact of FinTech on traditional banking. [A] /
  • [CO3]
  • FinTech refers to the use of innovative technolo gies such as mobile applications, artificial
  • intelligence, blockchain, and data analytics to deliver financial services. It aims to make
  • financial transactions faster, cheaper, and more convenient. FinTech companies provide
  • services like digital payments, online lending, robo-advisory, and peer-to-peer transfers. These
  • services operate with high efficiency and require minimal physical infrastructure.
  • FinTech has transformed customer expectations by offering instant and user-friendly services.
  • As a result, t raditional banks have been pressured to upgrade their technology and digital
  • platforms. Banks now focus more on mobile banking, online customer support, and digital
  • onboarding. FinTech also enhances financial inclusion by reaching unbanked and remote
  • populations.
  • However, FinTech competition challenges the profitability of traditional banks. Many banks
  • collaborate with FinTech firms to improve their service quality. FinTech promotes
  • transparency, better risk management, and personalized services through dat a analytics.
  • Overall, FinTech has modernized the financial sector by reshaping how banking services are
  • accessed and delivered.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the contemporary trends in banking / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the contemporary trends in banking. [U] / [CO4]
  • Modern banking is undergoing rapid transformation driven by technological advancements and
  • changing customer expectations. One major trend is digital banking, where most financial
  • services are provided through mobile apps and online platforms. Another trend is the rise of
  • UPI and instant payment systems, which have replaced traditional payment methods.
  • Banks are also adopting Artificial Intelligence for chatbots, fraud detection, and customer
  • analytics. Blockchain technology is being used for secure transactions and record -keeping.
  • Another important trend is open banking, which allows third-party service providers to access
  • banking data with customer consent.
  • The introduction of neo -banks—banks that operate fully online without branches —is also
  • reshaping financial services. Cybersecurity has gained importance as digital tra nsactions
  • increase. Banks are investing more in data protection and regulatory compliance.
  • Sustainable and green banking practices have also gained popularity due to environmental
  • concerns. Personalized financial products based on data analytics are becomi ng common.
  • Overall, contemporary banking focuses on speed, security, convenience, and customer-centric
  • services.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss in detail the services provided under corporate banking / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss in detail the services provided under corporate banking. [U] / [CO2]
  • Corporate banking provides specialized financial services to large companies, institutions, and
  • business clients. One of its major services is working capital finance, which helps businesses
  • manage day-to-day operational expenses. It also offers term loans for long -term investments
  • like machinery, infrastructure, and expansion.
  • Corporate banks provide cash management services to help companies manage collections,
  • payments, and liquidity efficiently. They also offer trade finance services such as letters of
  • credit and bank guarantees, which support domestic and international trade. Treasury and forex
  • services help firms manage currency risks and invest surplus funds wisely.
  • Corporate banking also includes syndicated loans, where multiple banks fund a large project
  • collectively. Overdraft and credit facilities provide quick access to short-term funds.
  • Banks also offer merchant banking and advisory services, including mergers, acquisitions, and
  • corporate restructuring. Custodial services are offered to manage securities and assets.
  • Insurance, derivatives, and investment p roducts are provided as part of corporate financial
  • planning. Overall, corporate banking ensures large businesses receive customized financial
  • solutions for smooth and efficient operations.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss in detail the functions of commercial bank / [CO1] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss in detail the functions of commercial bank. [U] / [CO1]
  • Commercial banks perform several essential functions to support individuals, businesses, and
  • the economy. Their primary function is accepting deposits, such as savings, current, and fixed
  • deposits. These deposits help mobilize public savings into produc tive use. Another major
  • function is granting loans and advances, including personal loans, business loans, and
  • overdrafts.
  • Banks also provide credit creation, where the lending process multiplies the money supply in
  • the economy. They offer payment and settlement services such as NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, cheque
  • clearing, and digital transfers. Commercial banks perform agency functions, like collecting
  • bills, paying taxes, and remitting funds on behalf of customers.
  • They provide investment services, including mutual funds, insurance distribution, and wealth
  • management. Banks also assist businesses with trade finance, foreign exchange, and letters of
  • credit.
  • Commercial banks maintain safe deposit lockers to ensure the security of valuables. They also
  • play a key role in economic development by providing credit to agriculture, industry, and small
  • enterprises.
  • Through monetary transmission, banks help implement the RBI’s monetary policy. Overall,
  • commercial banks support financial stability, promote savings, and facilitate smooth economic
  • activities.
